clue.text: Cents gathered by Spanish artist lie on cloth

indicators.note: coins gathered by a person are taken in and held within

parts.note: Joan Miró, the Catalan painter
C is the abbreviation for cents
a fib is a small lie
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A Spanish painter pockets small change while lying on a piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Microfibre is a synthetic fabric woven from very fine threads, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Great after switching halves in match

indicators.note: switching halves means the back half of the word is moved to the front

parts.note: a game is a match

explanation.surface: A football match that came good after the teams swapped ends at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching halves' sounds like teams changing ends at half-time; here the word's halves swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for great or brilliant.

clue.text: Look at summer destination in Iceland, say

parts.note: to check out is to look at
read as one who sums: something that counts or adds up

explanation.surface: Planning a holiday trip to Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceland is not the country here: it is a British chain of frozen-food supermarkets. 'Summer' is not the season but one who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers in a supermarket such as Iceland end up at the till where goods are paid for, their final stop.

clue.text: Belonging to force, one oddly cheery copper

parts.note: of expresses belonging
F is the abbreviation for force in physics
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions only

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A jolly constable who is part of the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A copper is British slang for a policeman, and an officer is a police officer.

clue.text: Superficially decorated home with large donation

parts.note: being in means being at home
L is the abbreviation for large
aid is help given, a donation

explanation.surface: A house spruced up cosmetically thanks to a big charitable gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid work has pieces set into its surface for ornament, so it is decorated at the surface.

clue.text: One attending comps upended vehicle? I … I'm not sure

indicators.note: in a down answer, upended means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ego is Latin for I, the self
er is the hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone entering competitions wondering whether the prize is a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comps' looks like competitions to enter for prizes; races are competitions too.
explanation.definitionFit: A racegoer attends race meetings, and races are competitions.

clue.text: Has no time for settlements

indicators.note: having no time means the letter standing for time is taken away from the word

parts.note: towns are settlements
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone too busy to bother with settling disputes, or with villages.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, so the verb is a synonym of has.

clue.text: Convulsive muscle was author's obvious facial feature

indicators.note: a convulsive movement is a violent spasm, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's face twitching with a muscle spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick, drooping one, hard to miss on any face.

clue.text: Stall on A11? Give way

parts.note: a stand is a market stall
taken as written
a side of eleven players, as in football or cricket

explanation.surface: A roadside stall on the A11 highway causing drivers to yield.
explanation.walkthrough: A11 looks like a British trunk road; split it into A and 11, and eleven players make a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand aside is to step out of the way, to yield to someone else.

clue.text: Happy having bear holding paw back

indicators.note: going back means the whole construction is read from right to left
one word holding another keeps it inside itself

parts.note: to lug is to carry or bear something heavy
to paw someone is to feel them clumsily

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful because a bear has its paw held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning carry, and the reversal applies to the whole construction, not just the inner word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleeful means full of delight and merriment, a close synonym of happy.

clue.text: Mark poorly inscribed in cut wood

indicators.note: something inscribed in a surface is written into it, so it sits within
a cut word has been shortened, here losing its final letter

parts.note: cedar is a fragrant timber
poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A clumsy mark carved into a sawn piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' looks like an adverb describing the carving, but it means unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the hooked diacritical mark under a letter c, as in façade, so it is a written mark.

clue.text: Funny person occupied by electric current turned physicist

indicators.note: turned means flipped round to read the other way
a place occupied by someone has them inside it

parts.note: a card is a comical, eccentric person
I is the physics symbol for current

explanation.surface: A comedian electrocuted and spun round becomes a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Dirac was a British theoretical physicist, a founder of quantum mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dirac was a Nobel prize-winning British theoretical physicist, so he is an example.

clue.text: Discussing doing nothing in particular

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to kick an idea around is to talk it over informally
second meaning: to be idling about with no purpose

explanation.surface: Chatting while idling about with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two idiomatic senses: debating an idea casually, and loafing aimlessly.

clue.text: Defeat in sports venues disheartened heavyweights

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second
disheartened means the heart, the central letter, is removed

parts.note: racecourses and golf courses are sports venues
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: Heavyweight boxers dispirited after losing in their arenas.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of a seven-letter word is its single middle letter, which goes before the defeat is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossuses are giants, figures of immense size or importance, so heavyweights in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Such work unfortunately going over day is overdue

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are in a bad order
read in reverse, the shuffled answer goes over, that is around, the letter for day; so that letter must come out

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A grumble about a piece of work that missed its deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite clue: the answer, shuffled with D inside it, makes OVERDUE. To solve, take D from OVERDUE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is a body of work, or a single piece of artistic work, taken from French.

clue.text: Embraces toyshop award between regularly emitted weeps

indicators.note: placed between means the pieces sit within the outer letters
letters emitted at regular intervals means every other one is let out

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters remain
the Early Learning Centre, a British chain of toyshops
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A child crying between the shelves of a toyshop and a prize-giving.
explanation.walkthrough: The Early Learning Centre is a British chain of toyshops; the Order of Merit is a British honour in the monarch's gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome a new idea or person is to embrace them warmly, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: University vexed German city dons

indicators.note: to don is to put on, as with clothing, so one word wears the other

parts.note: sore means annoyed or vexed
Bonn, former West German capital

explanation.surface: Academics at a university annoyed with a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers, which suits the surface, but it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the famous university in Paris.

clue.text: Company looking west, Japanese firm with new event

indicators.note: in an across answer, looking west means facing right to left

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
Casio makes watches and calculators
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A Japanese electronics maker launches a new product at a big western showcase.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular happening or special function, so it is a synonym of event.

clue.text: Raised large sum to secure frost-free rice paddy

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means read upwards, bottom to top
to secure something is to hold it fast within

parts.note: pots of money is a large amount

indicators.note: free of frost means that word is removed

parts.note: taken as written
frost is ice

explanation.surface: Money raised to protect a paddy field from frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rice paddy' reads as a field, but paddy is British slang for a fit of temper, as is strop.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy and a strop are both informal British words for a sulky fit of bad temper.

clue.text: Third of plants on verge flourish

indicators.note: the third of a word means only its third letter is taken

parts.note: the third letter of plants
a bound is a boundary, an edge or verge

explanation.surface: Plants growing on a roadside verge thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verge' suggests a grass strip by a road, but here it is the edge or limit of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in great numbers, to flourish and thrive in plenty.

clue.text: Caught second discharge of cone's sweet fare

indicators.note: something caught by the ear has been heard rather than seen

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
lava pours from a volcanic cone

explanation.surface: Catching a second helping of ice cream dribbling from its cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the cricket C, but it means heard; the cone is a volcano's.
explanation.definitionFit: Baklava is a sweet Middle Eastern pastry of filo, nuts and honey.

clue.text: Construction material engineer used on sides of lodge

parts.note: James Watt, Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters only

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An engineer choosing materials for the walls of a lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is woven sticks used, with daub, as a building material for walls.

clue.text: Maths symbol bookmaker initially inserted in even row

indicators.note: inserted in means placed inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: all square means level or even

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the first letter of bookmaker
a row is a din, a racket

explanation.surface: A betting man introduced into a quarrel about mathematics.
explanation.walkthrough: B is inserted between the two words of the phrase meaning even row.
explanation.definitionFit: Square brackets are punctuation used in mathematics to group terms, so it is a maths symbol.

clue.text: Simple measure to avoid powerful nation revolting

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters run the other way
the word must avoid those letters, so they are left out

parts.note: taken as written
the United States, a superpower

explanation.surface: A modest policy proposal designed to head off a superpower's uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The powerful nation must be turned round before it can be found and removed from the middle of the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means simple or nothing more than, as in a mere child.

clue.text: Determined to attack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: resolved or fixed on doing something

explanation.surface: Someone resolved on going on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set upon a plan means fixed on it; to set upon someone is to assault them.

clue.text: Portion banks withheld from merchants in conflict

indicators.note: with the banks, or outer edges, withheld, the word loses its first and last letters
letters in conflict are fighting each other and end up in disorder

parts.note: the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Banks hold back a share of funds from traders caught up in a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a slice or instalment, especially of money, so it is a portion.

clue.text: Swimmer leaving hot island

indicators.note: with hot leaving, its letter departs from the word

parts.note: a shark is a swimmer
H is the abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A swimmer getting out of the hot sea onto an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small car-free Channel Island, so it is an island by example.

clue.text: Look to bear north-east with winds from West Africa

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the first word carries the others inside it

parts.note: to see is to look
NE is the abbreviation for north-east
gales are strong winds

explanation.surface: Watching a bear in strong north-easterly winds blowing from West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it means carry, so the look word carries the rest inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegalese describes something from Senegal, a country in West Africa.
